feature1.prompt: __in doesn't clear selected fields on the RHS when QuerySet.alias() is used after annotate(). This issue causes an OperationalError indicating that a sub-select returns 10 columns instead of the expected 1.
feature1.hint_texts: This feature addresses the preparation of lookup queries in django/db/models/fields/related_lookups.py. The implementation should update the get_prep_lookup() method so that when alias() is chained after annotate(), the selected fields on the right‐hand side are properly configured. Instead of clearing the select clause or adding fields inappropriately, the code should use a method to set the field values correctly based on the target field. Make sure the logic distinguishes whether the lhs field is a primary key and then derives the appropriate field name to pass to the new setter.
feature1.entrypoint:
File: django/db/models/fields/related_lookups.py
Function: get_prep_lookup (around lines 90-107)
Modification: Replace the call to clear_select_clause() and add_fields() with a call to set_values([target_field]).

feature2.prompt: __in doesn't clear selected fields on the RHS when QuerySet.alias() is used after annotate(). This issue leads to an OperationalError because the sub-select returns an unexpected number of columns (10 instead of 1).
feature2.hint_texts: This feature focuses on how the query system tracks the state of selected fields. In django/db/models/sql/query.py, the Query class should be updated so that it no longer relies on the old property for determining if select fields are present. Instead, introduce a class-level attribute that is updated by the set_values() method. This change ensures that once alias() is applied after annotate(), the query correctly recognizes that the select fields have been modified, thereby preventing the OperationalError.
feature2.entrypoint:
File: django/db/models/sql/query.py
Class: Query (starting around lines 198 and following)
Modification: Remove the existing @property for has_select_fields and add a new class attribute initialized to False. Then ensure that the set_values() method updates has_select_fields to True when it is called.

collaboration_points.shared_resources: Both features modify core query construction components; Feature1 changes django/db/models/fields/related_lookups.py and Feature2 updates django/db/models/sql/query.py. They share the underlying query object and its handling of selected fields.
collaboration_points.integration_strategy: After implementation, integration tests should confirm that alias() and annotate() work together seamlessly. The lookup preparation logic in Feature1 must trigger the proper state changes in the Query class modified in Feature2, ensuring that the final SQL returns the correct number of columns.
collaboration_points.communication_needs: Developers need to coordinate on the shared behavior of the query system. Discussions should focus on how the modified lookup preparation (Feature1) interacts with the new tracking of select fields in the Query class (Feature2) to avoid conflicts and guarantee correct query construction.
